title: Eden Park: overview

description: Eden Park stands in Auckland, New Zealand: a 50,000-capacity venue opened in 1900, home to All Blacks. The All Blacks' fortress. Stadiums are the cathedrals of sport — concrete memory banks where generations experienced the same joys and heartbreaks. This database covers the ground's history, architecture, great events, and how to visit it.

title: History
d: Eden Park opened in 1900. The All Blacks' fortress..
definition: Eden Park opened in 1900. The All Blacks' fortress..
description: The history of Eden Park begins in 1900. The All Blacks' fortress. Like all great grounds, it has been rebuilt, renamed, and reborn — stands rising where terraces stood, roofs arriving decades after the first kick. Its timeline is the timeline of its tenants' triumphs and the city's love affair with the game.

title: Architecture
d: Eden Park holds about 50,000 spectators in its current configuration.
definition: Eden Park holds about 50,000 spectators in its current configuration.
description: The architecture of Eden Park: a 50,000-capacity bowl designed to trap noise and frame the action. Great stadium design balances sightlines, acoustics, and atmosphere — the steepest stands feel closest, the roofs hold the roar in. Renovations keep adding hospitality while trying not to dilute the soul.

title: The tenants
d: Eden Park is home to All Blacks.
definition: Eden Park is home to All Blacks.
description: Eden Park belongs to All Blacks — and to the fans who fill it. The tenant-club bond defines the ground's identity: the songs, the rituals, the expectation. When the team thrives the stadium shakes; when it struggles the old ground groans with it. You cannot separate the venue from its people.

title: Great matches
d: The greatest nights at Eden Park live in legend.
definition: The greatest nights at Eden Park live in legend.

Every old ground has a canon of such nights, and they are why the place matters: the stadium is the stage, but the drama is the point.

title: Finals hosted

definition: Eden Park has hosted major finals and showpiece events.
description: Showpiece events at Eden Park: cup finals, international tournaments, and one-off spectacles that put the ground on the world stage. Hosting a final is a civic honor — the city dresses up, the world watches, and the stadium joins the short list of venues that have seen it all.

title: Concerts and events
d: Eden Park doubles as a concert and event venue.
definition: Eden Park doubles as a concert and event venue.
description: Beyond sport, Eden Park hosts concerts, ceremonies, and mega-events — the biggest stages need the biggest rooms. The ground's event history reads like pop culture itself. Multi-use keeps the economics working, though purists always prefer the roar of a matchday to anything else.

title: Visiting guide
d: Visit Eden Park: tours, matchdays, and practical tips.
definition: Visit Eden Park: tours, matchdays, and practical tips.
description: Visiting Eden Park: stadium tours run most days, taking in the dressing rooms, the tunnel, and the dugout — book ahead in season. On matchdays arrive early, learn the songs, and respect the home ends. Auckland, New Zealand is best reached by public transport; driving on event days is for the patient.

title: Best seats
d: Where to sit at Eden Park for atmosphere, view, or value.
definition: Where to sit at Eden Park for atmosphere, view, or value.
description: Seats at Eden Park: behind the goal for the songs, halfway up the side for the tactical view, high corners for value. The famous ends have waiting lists measured in years; the family sections trade noise for comfort. Wherever you sit, the rule is the same — arrive early, stay late.

title: Attendance records
d: Eden Park's biggest crowds and what drew them.
definition: Eden Park's biggest crowds and what drew them.
description: The biggest crowds at Eden Park came for the biggest occasions — derbies, finals, and farewell games. The All Blacks' fortress. Capacity has changed with all-seater conversions and expansions, so records from different eras are not directly comparable. What endures is the noise: full houses here are famously loud.

title: Derbies

title: The future
